Deflation year (CPI < -1%): 5 of 100 years, all 1926-38 -> effectively 0 post-1945 under fiat/backstop regime; use ~1%/yr floor probability
Major single commodity (oil, gas, gold, copper, wheat) doubling within <=24 months: ~13 episodes / 100 yrs -> ~1.3 per decade, ~12%/yr; conditional on a supply shock or war, near-certain
Broad commodity index (CRB/GSCI-type) doubling within <=3 years: ~4 episodes (1972-74, 1978-80 energy-led, 2002-08 leg, 2020-22 from Covid trough) -> ~0.4 per decade, ~4%/yr

Commodity supercycle ignition (multi-year broad bull >100% real): ~3.5 per century -> ~1 per 29 yrs; each required demand regime-shift (war, dollar break, China, energy transition/underinvestment) not just a supply outage

Sector capex boom reaching >1% of GDP incremental spend then busting: ~5 per century (1920s utilities, 1970s energy, 1990s telecom, 2000s housing/China-materials, 2010s shale; 2020s AI pending) -> ~0.5 per decade; historical P(sector equity drawdown >50% within 3 yrs of capex/GDP peak) ~ 80% (4 of 5 completed cases; shale energy -65%)
Fed hiking cycle ending in recession within 2 years: ~10 of 13 postwar cycles ~ 75% (soft landings: 1966, 1984, 1995, arguably 2023-25)

10y real yield regime flip (crossing +/-1% and staying >3 yrs): ~7 flips per century -> beware models calibrated only on 2010s (-1% to +0.5%) — that decade is a 1-in-10 outlier, matched only by 1942-51
lessons_for_model: Capex booms are financed by the prevailing rate regime: every boom (1920s utilities, 1970s energy, 1990s telecom, 2000s materials/housing, 2010s shale, 2020s AI) launched when the sector's ROIC exceeded a falling or negative real cost of capital, and every bust was triggered when real rates rose OR the demand assumption broke — model the boom's mortality as f(real 10y change since boom start, sector FCF gap)

Timing asymmetry: capex/GDP peaks lag price/valuation peaks by 6-24 months (rigs peaked Dec 1981 after oil peaked Apr 1980; telecom capex peaked mid-2000 after Mar 2000; mining capex peaked 2012 after 2011 metals peak). Supply arriving after the demand peak is what converts a correction into a glut — build a 2-4 year supply-lag into the model

Financing-mix is the best late-cycle flag: booms start equity/cash-funded and end debt/vendor-financed/SPV-funded (1929 pyramids, 2000 vendor financing ~$25B, 2006 CDO machine, 2014 HY energy issuance ~15% of HY market, 2025 AI SPVs/neocloud debt). When boom-sector debt issuance share doubles, historical bust probability within 3 yrs > 70%
Inflation >5% is a cluster process, not i.i.d. — use a 2-state Markov chain (P(stay hot) ~0.65, P(enter hot | cool) ~0.04) rather than a flat 21% annual draw

Commodity doublings need a demand regime-shift plus prior underinvestment; a supply outage alone (1990 Gulf, 2005 Katrina) produces spikes that mean-revert <18 months. Distinguish these in the Monte Carlo: spike (12%/yr, mean-reverting) vs supercycle (4%/yr broad, persistent 8-12 yrs)

Credit blowout magnitude is regime-dependent: pre-1985 crunches were rate-level events (Baa 17%); modern ones are spread events (HY 800-2,200bp); post-2008, central-bank backstops truncate duration (2020: 6 weeks; 2023: 3 weeks) but not frequency — model shorter, sharper spread paths after 2008

The 2010s ZIRP decade is a 1-in-10 outlier (real 10y +0.3%, zero >5% inflation years, zero broad commodity doubling, longest-ever gap between >20% drawdowns 2009-2020) — a backtest calibrated 2010-2019 will understate every base rate above by roughly half

Valuation conditions but does not time: CAPE >30 occurred in 1929, 1997-2001, 2018-2026(ex-2022); subsequent 10y real equity returns from those levels averaged 0-3%/yr, and 3 of 4 completed episodes included a >45% drawdown — for the 2025-26 AI boom, prior odds of a >20% index drawdown within 5 yrs are ~70-80%, of a >50% boom-sector drawdown ~80%

Real-rate normalization (2022-26: TIPS ~+2%) historically ends commodity bears and starts capex discipline everywhere EXCEPT the one sector with a perceived demand regime-shift — that sector (AI now, telecom 1999, shale 2013) keeps spending into rising rates and absorbs the eventual glut

Regime transitions are policy-forced, not gradual: 1933, 1951, 1971, 1979, 2008, 2020 — jumps, not drifts. Use a regime-switching model with rare forced transitions (~0.7 per decade) rather than continuous mean-reversion in rates/inflation

macro.topic: 100-year quantitative map (1914-2026) of geopolitical shocks to markets and industrial supply chains — drawdowns, commodity moves, chokepoints, disruption durations, recovery times, and per-decade base rates for Monte Carlo shock priors

regimes.period: 1914-1945: Total-war era (market closures, physical blockade, price controls)
regimes.description: Great-power war twice in 31 years. Shocks were existential: exchanges closed outright, commodities were rationed, and blockade (not price) was the transmission mechanism. WWI: NYSE closed 31 Jul-12 Dec 1914 (4.5 months, longest ever); Dow fell ~24% on reopening day, then +82% in 1915 (best year on record) as the US became the Allied arsenal. Dardanelles closure cut off ~90% of Russian grain exports permanently; wheat roughly doubled 1914-17; Atlantic U-boat campaign drove tanker/freight rates up ~10x. WWII: Dow -25% in the two weeks of the Fall of France (May 1940), full peak-to-trough ~-40% (1939 to Apr 1942); bottom came at the moment of maximum peril (Apr 1942), then +130% to 1945. Japan's capture of Malaya/Dutch East Indies removed ~90% of natural rubber and much tin supply for ~3.5 years — solved by synthetic substitution (US synthetic rubber output 8,000t 1941 → 800,000t 1945), the century's clearest substitution precedent. Chokepoints: North Atlantic convoys, Suez (intermittently unusable 1940-43, Cape reroute), Malacca lost to Japan 1942-45. Real equity recovery in defeated/occupied countries: -90%+ (Germany, Japan) with 10-25 year real recovery; France/Italy similar in real terms via inflation.
numbers: NYSE closed 4.5 months 1914; Dow -24% reopening, +82% 1915
WWII Dow peak-to-trough -40%, France-fall fortnight -25%, bottom Apr 1942
Rubber: 90% of world supply lost 1942-45, synthetic substitution ~3 years
German/Japanese real equity losses >90%, 10-25 yr real recovery
Freight/tanker rates ~10x in U-boat campaigns

regimes.period: 1945-1971: Pax Americana / Bretton Woods (shocks shallow, recoveries fast)
regimes.description: US hegemony + spare capacity everywhere made geopolitical shocks brief price events. Korea (Jun 1950): S&P -12.9% in one month after invasion — fully recovered in ~3 months; the real shock was commodities: panic stockpiling drove wool +100%+, rubber and tin roughly 2x within a year, US CPI to 9.3% (1951); spike fully unwound by 1952. Suez 1956: canal blocked Nov 1956-Apr 1957 (5 months), cutting the route carrying ~2/3 of Europe's oil (~1.5 mb/d); European rationing, tanker rates ~3x, but crude posted prices barely moved because US spare capacity + Cape rerouting filled the gap; S&P dipped ~-8-10% (with Hungary), recovered in months. Suez closed again 1967-1975 (8 years!) — and the world barely noticed at first, because the supertanker/Cape system adapted; the lesson: closed chokepoints get engineered around, at a freight-cost premium of roughly 20-40%. Vietnam produced no acute market shock but its unfinanced fiscal expansion seeded the inflation that made the next regime's shocks lethal.
numbers: Korea: S&P -12.9% in 1 month, recovered in 3 months; wool/rubber/tin ~2x; CPI 9.3% 1951
Suez 1956: 5-month closure, 1.5 mb/d rerouted, tanker rates ~3x, equities -8-10%
Suez 1967-75: 8-year closure, absorbed via supertankers + Cape at ~20-40% freight premium
No US equity drawdown >15% attributable to geopolitics alone in this regime

regimes.period: 1971-1991: Oil-weapon era (commodity shocks meet monetary fragility — the fat-tail regime)
regimes.description: The only period where geopolitical shocks produced multi-year, economy-wide damage — because they hit an already-inflationary, post-gold monetary system. 1973 embargo (Oct 1973-Mar 1974, 5 months): Arab producers cut ~4.4 mb/d gross (~7% of world supply); oil $3→$12 (+300%); S&P 500 -48% Jan 1973-Oct 1974 (shock + Watergate + monetary regime break); nominal index recovery ~1976, real recovery not until ~1985 — the century's benchmark 'shock hits fragile macro' tail. 1979 Iranian revolution: ~4-5 mb/d Iranian output collapsed; spot crude $13→$34-40 (~2.5-3x) over 18 months; compounded by Iran-Iraq war outbreak (Sep 1980) removing another ~4 mb/d briefly; real oil price didn't normalize until the 1986 crash to $10. Tanker War 1984-88: 400+ ships attacked in the Gulf, war-risk insurance premia spiked, US reflagging convoys (Earnest Will) — yet oil FELL through the period because OPEC spare capacity was ~10 mb/d: chokepoint harassment without supply deficit does not move price. Gulf War 1990-91: Iraq+Kuwait 4.3 mb/d off market; Brent $17→$36 (+112%) in 10 weeks; S&P -19.9% Jul-Oct 1990; on the first night of Desert Storm oil fell 33% in one day and equities rallied — full S&P recovery ~4 months from trough. Hormuz was threatened in every one of these and never closed.
numbers: 1973: oil +300% in 5 months, 4.4 mb/d cut, S&P -48%, real equity recovery ~12 yrs
1979-80: oil ~2.7x over 18 months, 4-6 mb/d disrupted, real normalization 7 yrs (1986)
Tanker War: 400+ ship attacks 1984-88, oil price net NEGATIVE over period (spare capacity ~10 mb/d)
1990: oil +112% in 10 weeks, S&P -19.9% in 3 months, -33% oil in 1 day at war start, 4-month equity recovery
Hormuz: threatened 4x, closed 0x

regimes.description: Deep spare capacity, US naval dominance, hyper-globalized supply chains: every shock was shallow and fast. 9/11: NYSE closed 4 days (longest since 1933); S&P -11.6% in the reopening week, fully recovered in 19 trading days; airlines -40%+, insurance losses ~$40bn; oil spiked then fell on recession fear. Iraq 2003: the anxiety was worse than the war — S&P -14% Jan-Mar 2003, bottomed 9 days before invasion; oil $37→$28 within weeks of the start; Iraqi output (2.5 mb/d) took ~2 years to restore but markets never priced it. The regime's tail event was non-geopolitical (2008). But the seeds of the next regime were planted here: China 2010 rare-earth embargo on Japan (~2 months, after the Senkaku trawler incident) plus 40% export quota cut sent dysprosium from ~$300 to ~$2,500/kg and neodymium ~10x by mid-2011 — first modern demonstration of a materials monopoly weapon. Prices collapsed 80%+ by 2013 (demand destruction, stockpile release, Lynas/Molycorp entry); diversification of mining took ~5 years, but China retained ~90% of refining — the half-fixed problem that returns in 2025.
numbers: 9/11: 4-day closure, S&P -11.6%, recovery 19 trading days
Iraq 2003: pre-war S&P -14%, bottom 9 days pre-invasion; oil -25% on war start; Iraqi supply recovery ~2 yrs
REE 2010-11: Dy ~8x, Nd ~10x in 12 months; 2-month embargo; price collapse -80% by 2013; mining diversification 5 yrs; refining still ~90% China
Crimea 2014 (transition marker): MICEX -10% in a day, ruble -40% over 2014, wheat +20% for 2 months, S&P <-2% — first weaponized-finance sanctions

regimes.period: 2014-2026: Weaponized interdependence (sanctions, export controls, chokepoint harassment return)
regimes.description: Great-power competition resumes; the weapon of choice is the network chokepoint (finance, energy, semiconductors, critical minerals) rather than blockade. Ukraine 2022: Brent $78→$128 (+64%); TTF gas peaked €345/MWh Aug 2022 (~10x pre-crisis norm; Russia had supplied 40% of EU gas — replaced by LNG in ~18 months, Nord Stream sabotaged Sep 2022); CBOT wheat +70% to all-time high (Russia+Ukraine ~28% of exports; Odesa blocked; normalized ~14 months via grain corridor + harvest cycle); LME nickel +250% in 2 days forcing exchange suspension and trade cancellation; palladium record $3,440; Ukraine's ~50% share of semiconductor-grade neon (Ingas/Cryoin) went offline — prices 5x+ but ZERO fab stoppages because chipmakers held ~6 months inventory and recycled. S&P attributable dip ~-7 to -13% (Feb-Mar), Europe -20%; $300bn Russian reserves frozen — the financial-weaponization high-water mark. US chip controls (Oct 2022, tightened Oct 2023/Dec 2024/2025): Nvidia -8.5% on announcement day, $5.5bn H20 writedown Apr 2025, later partially reversed by the 15%-revenue-share license deal; SOX 2022 drawdown -46% but mostly rate-cycle. China retaliation ladder, each step ~6-15 months after a US move: Ga/Ge licensing Aug 2023 (China: 98%/60% of supply; gallium ~2x to $600+/kg, germanium ~2x+), antimony Sep 2024 (~3x, $12k→$39k/t), outright Ga/Ge/Sb ban on US Dec 2024, rare-earth magnet licensing Apr 2025 (magnet exports -75% in May 2025; Ford Chicago and European auto lines halted within ~8 weeks — inventory buffers for magnets were weeks, not months). Red Sea 2023-25: Houthi attacks cut Suez transits ~50%, Shanghai-Europe container rates ~5x briefly, +10-14 days via Cape — trade rerouted, no goods shortage. Taiwan Strait: ~90% of leading-edge (<5nm) foundry capacity in Taiwan, ~40%+ of container fleet transits annually; Aug 2022 and 2024-25 exercises moved markets <2% — the largest unpriced tail in the dataset.
numbers: 2022: gas 10x (18-mo normalization), wheat +70% (14-mo), Brent +64% (12-mo), nickel +250%/2 days, neon 5x with 0 fab stoppages (6-mo buffers)
$300bn reserves frozen; SWIFT cutoffs
Ga +~100%, Ge +~100%, Sb +~200% within 6-12 months of controls; magnet exports -75% May 2025, auto stoppages in ~8 weeks
Red Sea: Suez transits -50% for 12+ months, container rates ~5x peak, +10-14 days rerouting, no shortage
Taiwan: 90% leading-edge chips, priced at <2% index moves on each escalation

key_numbers: Equity drawdown from PURE geopolitical shocks (no macro amplifier): median ~-8 to -13%, range -5% to -20% (Korea -12.9%, 9/11 -11.6%, Gulf buildup -19.9%, Ukraine ~-7 to -13%, Cuba -7%)
Equity drawdown when shock hits fragile macro regime: -40% to -55% nominal (1973-74: -48%; 1939-42: -40%), real recovery 10-25 years; defeated-country equities -90%+

Equity recovery time, pure shocks: 1-4 months (9/11: 19 days; Korea: 3 months; Gulf War: 4 months from trough); markets historically bottom AT or just before hostilities begin (Apr 1942, Jan 1991, Mar 2003)
Oil shock magnitudes: 1973 +300%/5 months; 1979 +170%/18 months; 1990 +112%/10 weeks; 2022 +64%/6 weeks — declining severity as supply diversified and strategic reserves grew
Physical oil disruption sizes: 4-6 mb/d in every major event (1973, 1979, 1980, 1990) ≈ 5-9% of world supply; replaced by spare capacity in 3-9 months whenever spare > disruption

Niche-material shocks are the biggest % movers: neon 5-10x (2022), dysprosium 8x (2011), gas 10x (2022), antimony 3x (2024), gallium/germanium 2x (2023-24) — but index impact near zero; damage is sectoral and shows up 1-3 quarters later
Inventory buffer determines whether a supply cut is a price event or a production stoppage: neon 6 months (no stoppage), rare-earth magnets ~6-8 weeks (auto lines halted 2025), oil SPR 90+ days

Supply-chain diversification times: oil via spare capacity 3-9 months; LNG rerouting 18 months; wheat one harvest cycle 12-14 months; rare-earth MINING 5 years; rare-earth REFINING >15 years and counting (China ~90% 2010 and ~85-90% 2025); leading-edge fabs 4-6+ years per fab

Chokepoint throughput at risk: Hormuz ~20-21 mb/d (~20% of oil, no substitute pipeline capacity beyond ~6-8 mb/d); Malacca ~16 mb/d + ~30-40% of world trade; Suez ~12-15% of trade (closed 1956-57 for 5 months, 1967-75 for 8 years, degraded 50% 2023-25); Taiwan Strait: 90% leading-edge semiconductors, no rerouting possible
Hormuz base rate: threatened/attacked in 1973, 1980-88, 1990, 2011-12, 2019, 2024-25 — actually closed: 0 times in 100 years (harassment premium 5-25% on crude, decays in weeks)

Chokepoint closure gets engineered around at a 20-40% freight premium in 2-12 months (Cape reroutes 1967, 2024) — EXCEPT where the chokepoint is a monopoly production site (Taiwan fabs, Chinese refining), where no reroute exists
Export-control retaliation lag: 6-18 months per rung (Oct 2022 chips → Aug 2023 Ga/Ge → Dec 2024 ban → Apr 2025 magnets)
One-day event repricing: oil -33% on Desert Storm day 1; nickel +250% over 2 days 2022; Nvidia -8.5% on Oct 2022 controls; MICEX -10% on Crimea day
base_rates: Great-power direct war (peer militaries in sustained combat: WWI, WWII, Korea US-China): 3 events / 11.2 decades ≈ 0.27 per decade ≈ 2.5-3% per year unconditional — but regime-conditional: ~0.6/decade in multipolar eras (1914-45), ~0.1/decade under clear hegemony (1945-2013); for 2026-2035 a multipolar-conditioned prior of 4-6% per year is defensible

Regional war materially disrupting a key commodity (Suez 56, Six-Day 67, Yom Kippur 73, Iran revolution 79, Iran-Iraq 80, Gulf 90, Iraq 03, Libya 11, Ukraine 22, Red Sea/Houthi 23, Israel-Iran 25): ~11 events / 11.2 decades ≈ 1.0 per decade ≈ 9-10% per year; clustered — Poisson underestimates, use ~0.6 baseline with 2-3x multiplier during active-rivalry regimes

Embargo / export-control escalation with market-moving effect (US-Japan oil 1941, Iran nationalization 1951, Arab embargoes 1967 & 1973, US grain embargo 1980, COCOM tightenings, REE 2010, Russia sanctions 2014, Russia mega-sanctions + chip controls 2022, Ga/Ge 2023, Sb + bans 2024, REE magnets 2025): ~13 events / 11.2 decades ≈ 1.2 per decade long-run, but 5-6 per decade at post-2018 run-rate — use regime-switching prior: 0.5/decade (cooperative), 4-6/decade (competitive, current)

Major chokepoint physically closed or throughput -50%+ for >1 month (Suez 1956, Suez 1967-75, Red Sea 2023-25): ~3 events / 11.2 decades ≈ 0.27 per decade; Hormuz-specific closure: 0/11.2 decades despite ~6 threat episodes — model Hormuz as high-threat/low-closure: threat episode ~0.5/decade, closure|threat ~5-10%, closure duration if it happens: weeks not years (all parties' revenue depends on reopening)

Equity drawdown >15% attributable primarily to geopolitics: ~4 events (1914, 1940, 1973, 1990) / 11.2 decades ≈ 0.35 per decade — geopolitics alone rarely produces bear markets; conditional on shock coinciding with inflationary/fragile macro, P(drawdown >30%) roughly triples

Commodity price spike >100% within 12 months from a geopolitical trigger: ~8 events (1917 wheat, 1950-51, 1973, 1979, 1990, 2010-11 REE, 2022 gas/wheat/nickel, 2024-25 Sb/REE) ≈ 0.7 per decade for SOME commodity; for oil specifically ≈ 0.35/decade
Exchange closure / trading suspension: 1914 (4.5 months), 1933, 2001 (4 days), LME nickel 2022 (8 days) ≈ 0.3 per decade — nonzero prior on 'you cannot trade out of the shock'
lessons_for_model: Distribution is bimodal, not lognormal: ~85% of geopolitical shocks are mean-reverting blips (equities -5 to -20%, recovery 1-4 months); ~15% interact with a fragile macro/monetary regime and become fat tails (-40 to -90% real, 10-25 yr recovery). Model as a mixture: shock severity should be conditioned on a 'macro fragility' state variable (inflation trend, fiscal room, spare capacity), not drawn independently.

Commodity moves exceed equity moves by 3-15x in every event. The transmission to equities is lagged 2-4 quarters via margins and CPI. Simulate the commodity leg first, equity leg as a damped, lagged function of it.

Spare capacity / inventory coverage is the single best predictor of shock amplitude: 4-6 mb/d oil outages produced +300% in 1973 (no spare) and +64% in 2022 (SPR + shale); identical neon-scale cuts produced zero stoppages with 6-month buffers (2022) and auto-line halts with 6-week buffers (2025 magnets). Prior on price impact should scale ~inversely with (buffer months + spare capacity %).

Threat is not closure: Hormuz has a 100-year record of maximal threat and zero closure. Assign chokepoint-closure probabilities per chokepoint, not generically; reserve the no-reroute catastrophic branch for monopoly production nodes (Taiwan leading-edge fabs, Chinese REE refining), where 'recovery time' is 4-15 years, not months.

Markets bottom at the outbreak, not the peak, of hostilities (Apr 1942, Jan 1991, Mar 2003): uncertainty resolution is worth more than the war costs. In simulation, place max drawdown in the pre-war/escalation phase and begin recovery at commencement — except when the war itself destroys the supply (1973, 2022 gas).

Recovery clocks by asset: equities 1-4 months (pure shock); food one harvest cycle (12-14 mo); energy 6-24 mo (rerouting/LNG/spare capacity); niche minerals 3-5 yrs (mining) to >15 yrs (refining); semiconductors 4-6 yrs per fab. Use these as distinct recovery-time distributions per shock type.

Export-control escalation is an autocorrelated ladder, not i.i.d.: each move draws retaliation in 6-18 months, and the post-2018 event rate (4-6/decade) is ~4x the century average. Model embargo frequency as regime-switching (cooperative vs competitive) with the current state firmly competitive; also allow partial reversals (2010 REE collapse, 2025 Nvidia license deal) — controls leak and get traded away ~30-50% of the time within 2 years.

Financial-infrastructure weaponization (SWIFT cutoff, $300bn reserve freeze, exchange trade cancellation) is a post-2014 shock channel with no earlier analogue except 1914's closures: include a nonzero probability (~0.3/decade) that the market mechanism itself is suspended and mark-to-market is impossible for days-to-months.

Base-rate clustering: events arrive in regime clusters (1914-45, 1973-90, 2014-), not uniformly. A Monte Carlo using unconditional Poisson rates will understate decade-level variance; use a two-state (calm/rivalry) hidden Markov process where rivalry multiplies all event intensities 2-5x, with regime persistence of 10-30 years.

The largest current mispricing per the historical pattern: Taiwan Strait combines the highest concentration ever recorded for a critical input (90% leading-edge logic, no substitute for 4-6+ years) with the smallest observed market reaction to escalation (<2%). Historical analogues (rubber 1942, neon 2022) say concentration this extreme resolves via multi-year substitution at 5-10x price — a Taiwan conflict scenario should carry semiconductor price multipliers of 3-10x, tech-sector drawdowns in the 1973-class (-40%+) branch, and recovery times of 5+ years, i.e., it belongs in the fat-tail mixture component, not the blip component.
